The mass of these yolk-dependent prolarvae is remarkably low, with a wet weight at birth of only 0.0018 grams [Wwb = 0.0018 grams], reflecting the limited yolk reserves available at the moment of chorion rupture. This initial body mass is derived from an estimated egg diameter of approximately 1.5 millimeters, a value taken from the closely related species Chondrostoma nasus, though direct measurements for C. holmwoodii eggs are still forthcoming.
